newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremen cotton market boosted by higher yarn prices.
newsitem.headline: Bremen cotton market boosted by higher yarn prices.

text.p: Northwest Europe raw cotton prices rose as spinners achieved better yarn sales prices and as the effect of European Union anti-dumping duties was felt, the Bremen Cotton Exchange said on Thursday.
"Sustained firmness in cents and mark prices also boosted future market prospects," the Exchange wrote in a weekly market report, noting industry buying and positive sentiment.
The EU in November imposed dumping duties averaging 20 percent on grey cotton fabric from Asia and the Middle East.
Buyers in Bremen needed large nearby replacement material across the quality spectrum, the report said.
But reduced Central Asian availability and some logistics problems limited offers, especially in premium grades.
Upland deals were struck in West African descriptions, including Chad, for dates up to third quarter 1997.
Other transactions included Syrian, Spanish and Turkish cotton for first quarter 1997, as well as Israel-Acala, U.S./Texas and Iran cotton for first half 1997.
Long staple markets featured trades in Egyptian Giza 75/86 and Sudan-Barakat through first half 1997 as well as demand for materials from the U.S., Israel and Peru for the same dates.
Bremen cotton stocks on December 19 were 29,702 bales, down by 2,642 from last week and compared with 39,579 bales a year earlier.
Central Asia standard 1, 31-32 mm (value middling 1.1/16), was quoted at 85.50 cents per lb on December 12 compared with 83.00 on November 28 and 80.50 on November 14.
